summary.text: A Japanese boy with congenital ichthyosis, born at 37 weeks as one of fraternal twins, developed epilepsy, dysphagia, cortical blindness, quadriplegia and developmental delay after a rotavirus infection at 1 year 7 months and had food allergies. After hernia and cryptorchidism surgeries under general anesthesia, he was referred at 2 years 9 months for dental treatment of severe caries.

At the first visit he measured 78 cm and 9.08 kg, with whole-body scaling and dry skin, severe caries of the primary teeth, gingivitis, and wheelchair dependence; he could not cooperate. Netherton syndrome was suspected and SPINK5 sequencing showed no coding-region mutation; whole-exome sequencing at 7 years 1 month found ALOX12B candidate variants.

After assessment by a pediatrician, dermatologist and anesthesiologist, caries was treated in three general anesthesia sessions at 3 years 2 months, six weeks later and 3 years 8 months, the third delayed by pneumonia. Treatment included pulp removal, canal obturation, strip and stainless-steel crowns and composite restorations; he recovered uneventfully and was discharged without complications.

Monthly follow-up showed improved gingivitis and no caries at 4 years 7 months. Rough perioral skin after 2% APF improved after a neutral fluoride, and suspected candidiasis resolved with antifungal syrup. At 5 years 10 months a lower primary central incisor showed severe mobility and the exfoliating teeth were removed; permanent teeth erupted, pulpectomy-treated teeth exfoliated normally and no cavities were found through mixed dentition.

article_limitations: Figure pixels are described in visual.json; the annotation figures keep caption-layer status not_inspected.
The introduction age (2 years 6 months) differs from the referral and initial examination age (2 years 9 months); both kept, the introduction age as review-only.
Supplementary Table S1 (per-tooth diagnoses and restorations) and Supplementary Figure S1 are in the DOCX supplement and reviewed in its sidecar, not in this annotation.
Causes the authors only believe or suggest (hypersalivation, ionic beverages, candidiasis and nail changes, ALOX12B nonsense mutation and severe conditions) are not recorded as facts.
Several signs are untimed because their own sentences state no time; the first-visit time is not borrowed for them.
